fact: Pierce Brown wrote 'Red Rising' while living in his publisher’s garage, working tirelessly to refine the story before it was published.
'Red Rising' is heavily inspired by Roman mythology and history, with the ruling 'Golds' modeling their society after the Roman Republic and Empire.
The protagonist, Darrow, is a 'Red'—the lowest caste in the color-coded society—who undergoes a transformation to infiltrate the elite 'Gold' ruling class.
Pierce Brown originally wrote 'Red Rising' as a screenplay before deciding to adapt it into a novel.
The series has often been compared to 'The Hunger Games' and 'Game of Thrones' due to its mix of dystopian rebellion and brutal political intrigue.
Pierce Brown was rejected by over 120 literary agents before finally landing a deal for 'Red Rising.'
'Red Rising' has been adapted into a successful board game by Stonemaier Games, allowing players to explore the world’s factions and strategies.
Universal Pictures originally secured the film rights to 'Red Rising,' but after years of delays, Pierce Brown announced plans for a TV adaptation instead.
The series’ famous rebel group, 'Sons of Ares,' has a prequel comic series that explores their origins.
The name 'Lykos,' the mining colony where Darrow comes from, is derived from the Greek word for 'wolf,' which aligns with his leadership of the 'Howlers.'
